CHAPTER 2
ABOUT ORGANIZATION
2.1 About GAIL (India) Limited
GAIL (India) Limited is a Maharatna Central Public Sector Undertaking under the 
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, Government of India, headquartered in New 
Delhi. It is India's leading natural gas company, with an integrated presence across the 
entire natural gas value chain, covering transmission and marketing of natural gas, 
production and marketing of LPG and other liquid hydrocarbons, LPG transmission, 
petrochemicals, city gas distribution, and LNG regasification. GAIL operates one of the 
largest networks of natural gas pipelines in the country, spanning more than thirteen 
thousand kilometres, along with LPG pipelines covering over two thousand kilometres.
Figure 2.1: GAIL (India) Limited Logo — Insert Image Here
This internship was carried out at the GAIL Complex in Vijaipur, located in the Guna 
district of Madhya Pradesh, roughly one hundred and ninety kilometres from Bhopal 
and two hundred and sixty kilometres from Indore. The Vijaipur complex grew 
alongside the historic Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur (HVJ) natural gas pipeline and today 
houses two Gas Processing Units that extract LPG and other liquid hydrocarbons from 
natural gas. In recent years the complex has also become a site for GAIL's clean energy 
initiatives, hosting the country's first ten megawatt green hydrogen electrolyzer, capable 
of producing hydrogen through electrolysis using renewable power, along with one of 
the earliest Small Scale LNG skids commissioned in India.
Being a facility of this scale and complexity, Vijaipur handles continuous process 
operations involving pressurized gas, rotating machinery, and electrical systems, all of 
which carry safety considerations that field staff and safety personnel must track 
closely. It was within this operational context that the need for a faster, digital hazard 
reporting workflow was identified, forming the basis for the project undertaken during 
this internship.
2.2 Work Culture
GAIL's work culture at the Vijaipur complex is shaped strongly by the nature of its 
operations. Safety is treated as a shared responsibility rather than the concern of a single 
department, and employees across engineering, operations, and administrative 
functions are expected to be alert to hazards within their area of work. Structured shift 
patterns are followed in the process areas, supported by defined reporting and escalation 
procedures for anything from routine maintenance observations to safety critical events.
Interns and new employees are typically attached to a mentor or supervisor from the 
relevant department, who guides them through the facility's procedures and reviews 
their work at regular intervals. Cross functional coordination is common, since a single 
1

reported concern, such as a suspected leak or an equipment fault, is often examined 
jointly by the operations, maintenance, and safety teams before being closed out. 
Regular training sessions and toolbox talks are held to keep staff updated on safety 
protocols and any changes to standard operating procedures.
During the course of this internship, the intern was placed under the [Insert Department 
Name] department for the duration of the project, working under the guidance of [Insert 
Supervisor Name]. Regular reviews were held to align the reporting system being 
developed with the actual hazard categories and escalation flow used by the safety desk 
at Vijaipur.
2.3 Management Hierarchy
GAIL (India) Limited is governed by a Board of Directors headed by a Chairman and 
Managing Director, currently Shri Deepak Gupta, who oversees the company's overall 
strategy and operations. The Chairman and Managing Director is supported by a set of 
whole time Functional Directors responsible for areas such as Marketing and Business 
Development, Finance, Human Resources, and Projects, along with government 
nominee and independent directors on the Board.
At the facility level, the Vijaipur complex is headed by a senior Executive Director or 
Unit Head who reports into the corporate structure and is responsible for the day to day 
running of the plant. Reporting into this position is a set of departmental heads covering 
Production and Operations, Mechanical and Electrical Maintenance, Instrumentation, 
Fire and Safety, Human Resources and Administration, and Information Technology. 
Each department follows its own internal reporting line, with junior engineers and 
officers reporting to section heads, who in turn report to the respective department head.
This layered structure ensures that a hazard reported from the field passes through a 
clear, accountable chain, from the reporting employee, to the relevant department, to the 
safety desk, and, where necessary, up to facility leadership. The system developed 
during this internship was designed to mirror this same chain digitally, replacing what 
was previously a manual, multi step communication process with a single, centralized 
record that all relevant parties can access immediately.
2

Being a facility of this scale and complexity, Vijaipur handles continuous process 
operations involving pressurized gas, rotating machinery, and electrical systems, all of 
which carry safety considerations that field staff and safety personnel must track 
closely. It was within this operational context that the need for a faster, digital hazard 
reporting workflow was identified, forming the basis for the project undertaken during 
this internship.
2.2 Work Culture
GAIL's work culture at the Vijaipur complex is shaped strongly by the nature of its 
operations. Safety is treated as a shared responsibility rather than the concern of a single 
department, and employees across engineering, operations, and administrative 
functions are expected to be alert to hazards within their area of work. Structured shift 
patterns are followed in the process areas, supported by defined reporting and escalation 
procedures for anything from routine maintenance observations to safety critical events.
Interns and new employees are typically attached to a mentor or supervisor from the 
relevant department, who guides them through the facility's procedures and reviews 
their work at regular intervals. Cross functional coordination is common, since a single

2.3 Management Hierarchy
GAIL (India) Limited is governed by a Board of Directors headed by a Chairman and 
Managing Director, currently Shri Deepak Gupta, who oversees the company's overall 
strategy and operations. The Chairman and Managing Director is supported by a set of 
whole time Functional Directors responsible for areas such as Marketing and Business 
Development, Finance, Human Resources, and Projects, along with government 
nominee and independent directors on the Board.
At the facility level, the Vijaipur complex is headed by a senior Executive Director or 
Unit Head who reports into the corporate structure and is responsible for the day to day 
running of the plant. Reporting into this position is a set of departmental heads covering 
Production and Operations, Mechanical and Electrical Maintenance, Instrumentation, 
Fire and Safety, Human Resources and Administration, and Information Technology. 
Each department follows its own internal reporting line, with junior engineers and 
officers reporting to section heads, who in turn report to the respective department head.
This layered structure ensures that a hazard reported from the field passes through a 
clear, accountable chain, from the reporting employee, to the relevant department, to the 
safety desk, and, where necessary, up to facility leadership. The system developed 
during this internship was designed to mirror this same chain digitally, replacing what 
was previously a manual, multi step communication process with a single, centralized 
record that all relevant parties can access immediately.
